battle.name: 南高盧戰爭
battle.theater: 南高盧行省與利古里亞海岸山地
battle.brief: 前225年，第二次布匿戰爭的北翼開到南高盧：執政官軍沿海追打利古里人，卻在波河平原入口被波伊人與越嶺的蓋爾人聯軍擋住。卡面的希臘重步兵並非本役裝備，方陣的影子卻仍在羅馬軍團的縱隊裡：標槍齊射、退入主力、劍盾相接，手握長矛的經驗在山地里被改寫成楔形推進。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 南高盧戰爭是公元前225年羅馬共和國在第二次布匿戰爭北翼打的一場戰爭，主戰場是羅馬的南高盧行省（高盧行省）與其背後的利古里亞山地。開戰的一方是羅馬：前225年由執政官盧基烏斯·波斯圖米烏斯·阿爾比努斯與蓋烏斯·盧塔提烏斯·卡圖盧斯分率兩支執政官軍，每軍以兩個公民兵團為核心，輔以拉丁同盟的盟軍與高盧、希臘、西班牙的輔兵；羅馬在南高盧的盟友是希臘城邦馬西利亞（馬賽）及其殖民地埃姆波里翁、羅德、尼卡與阿加忒，馬西利亞在此前已屢次向羅馬求援，是把羅馬拖進這場山區戰爭的關鍵。另一方沒有國家，只有聯盟：波河平原的因蘇布列人與波伊人起兵，與翻越阿爾卑斯山的蓋爾人匯合；沿海山地的利古里人則以游擊與山道襲擊應戰。羅馬在意大利的戰線上還有漢尼拔的迦太基軍，漢尼拔的使者與高盧傭兵從北面牽制，使南高盧的戰事與主戰場連成一體。
countriesEn: The war in southern Gaul of 225 BC was one front of the Second Punic War fought by the Roman Republic, with the main theatre the province of Gallia Narbonensis and the Ligurian mountains behind it. On one side stood Rome: in 225 BC the consuls Lucius Postumius Albinus and Gaius Lutatius Catulus each commanded an army of two citizen legions backed by the contingents of the Latin League and by Gallic, Greek and Spanish auxiliaries; Rome's ally in the province was the Greek city of Massalia (Marseille) together with its colonies Emporion, Rhode, Nikaia and Agathe, and Massalia, which had called on Roman help repeatedly in the years before 225 BC, was the reason a Roman army was tied down in a mountain war. The other side had no state at all, only a coalition: the Insubres and the Boii of the Po plain rose in revolt and joined the Gauls who had come over the Alps, while the Ligurians of the coastal mountains answered with skirmishing and ambushes along their tracks. On the Italian front the same war had the Carthaginians of Hannibal, whose envoys and Gallic auxiliaries kept the northern pressure on, tying the southern Gaulian front into a single conflict with the main theatre.
people: 羅馬方面，前225年的兩位執政官是盧基烏斯·波斯圖米烏斯·阿爾比努斯與蓋烏斯·盧塔提烏斯·卡圖盧斯。阿爾比努斯三度出任執政官，前223年在前波伊人與因蘇布列人時大勝並俘獲七百五十人，前222年又奪下克拉斯提迪烏姆，是南高盧戰線三年裡唯一貫穿始終的指揮官。卡圖盧斯的戰歷更特別：前242年他在埃加迪亞群島打敗迦太基海軍，前225年卻在利古里亞的山脊之間打了一年仗，前231年出任監察官，兩場戰役一在海上、一在山中，隔著三十多年。迦太基的漢尼拔本人從未到過南高盧，但他派出的使者、錢財與高盧傭兵是波伊人敢於起兵的底氣。希臘一方沒有留下可考的名字：馬西利亞的使者、埃姆波里翁的商船都寫在事件裡而不寫在人名上。史料唯一留下姓名的敵方是李維筆下被消滅的法比烏斯家族——前225年三百零六名法比烏斯族人在克雷梅拉河峽谷全滅，是這場戰爭最沉重的一筆，也提醒讀者不要把李維的家族敘事當成實戰報告。
peopleEn: On the Roman side the consuls of 225 BC were Lucius Postumius Albinus and Gaius Lutatius Catulus. Albinus, consul three times, won a large victory over the Boii and the Insubres in 223 BC and took seven hundred and fifty prisoners, and in 222 BC seized Clastidium; he was the one commander who ran through all three years of the southern Gaulian line. Catulus's record is stranger still: he had beaten the Carthaginian fleet at the Aegadian Islands in 242 BC, and in 225 BC spent a campaigning season fighting between the ridges of Liguria; he later served as censor in 231 BC. Hannibal himself never set foot in southern Gaul, but his envoys, his money and his Gallic auxiliaries were the reason the Boii dared to rise. The Greek side left no name that can be checked: the envoys of Massalia and the merchant ships of Emporion appear in the events but not in the names. The only enemy the sources name is the Fabii, destroyed at the Cremera in Livy's narrative, where three hundred and six members of the clan perished in a gorge in 225 BC — the heaviest single loss of this front, and a reminder that Livy's family story is not a battle report.
kits: 卡面的希臘重步兵是本役的對照物而不是戰場實物。公元前500年前後定型於希臘城邦的重步兵，配圓形藤盾（aspis）、青銅胸甲與長矛（dory），方陣的正面靠盾牌互相遮蔽形成；到前225年，這套東西在希臘本土已被馬其頓的長槍方陣取代，在西地中海則退成雇佣兵與民兵的地方傳統。真正在利古里亞作戰的是羅馬軍團的縱隊：重裝步兵持橢圓大盾（scutum）、短劍與標槍（pilum），在手握式標槍於數十步外齊射，拋完退為百夫長率領的主力，再以劍盾接戰；兩翼的騎兵、投槍手與馬西利亞提供的希臘式輕裝部隊負責擾亂。利古里人自備小型圓盾（parma）、標槍與短刀，多不披甲，在林地與石坡上展開；蓋爾人與波伊人用寬大平盾與長劍，結成密集的部落縱隊進攻，沒有操練，也沒有希臘式的盾牆。糧秣靠海運：羅馬以馬西利亞與沿岸港口為基地，前222年更沿利古里亞海岸新闢一條軍用道路，把戰線貼著海走，避開長距離的內陸補給。山地作戰用得著的是繩索、斧頭、柴薪與投石索，而不是攻城塔。
kitsEn: The hoplite on the card is a foil, not a piece of equipment that fought here. The heavy infantry of the Greek cities, defined around 500 BC, carried the round wicker shield (aspis), a bronze cuirass and the long spear (dory), and the face of a phalanx was made solid by overlapping shields; by 225 BC that system had been superseded in Greece by the Macedonian pike phalanx and in the western Mediterranean survived only as a local tradition among mercenaries and militia. What actually fought in Liguria was the Roman cohort: heavy infantry with the large oval scutum, the gladius and the pilum, throwing javelins by the hundred at a distance of a few dozen paces, falling back behind the line of the principes, and closing in sword against shield; cavalry, skirmishers and Greek-style light troops supplied by Massalia covered the flanks. The Ligurians carried the small round parma, javelins and short swords, usually without armour, and fought from woodland and rocky slopes; the Gauls and the Boii used broad flat shields and long swords and came forward in dense tribal columns, undrilled and without any Greek shield wall. Supply came by sea: Rome used Massalia and the coastal ports as its base, and in 222 BC opened a military road along the Ligurian coast so that the front could move with the sea on its flank instead of depending on a long inland line. What the mountains actually called for were ropes, axes, firewood and slings, not siege towers.
tactics: 羅馬的戰術核心是縱隊制。軍隊以兩列縱隊前進，密集的前排不是希臘方陣的連續盾牆，而是由若干百人隊組成的可變陣形；前排標槍手在敵我進至二十步上下齊射，隨即退入主力隊伍身後，敵軍一旦逼近，第一線以劍盾相接，第二線再頂上，兩列縱隊交替掩護。遇上山地，前223至前222年的高盧戰役裡，執政官阿爾比努斯改用楔形（cuneus）推進：密集縱隊以連續縱深撞開對手，適用於利古里亞的狹窄谷道與起伏坡地。李維記載，前222年那一季羅馬在利古里亞連打九場，一路由沿海丘陵打到山營，最後以夜襲奪下敵營，縱火焚其器材而全軍退出，避免正面硬撞。敵方蓋爾人與波伊人的戰法正好相反：他們結成密集的縱隊一齊壓上，長劍繞過盾緣砍入，羅馬應對之道是標槍齊射加密集縱隊，而不是展開成線。最大的變數是補給：南高盧前線與意大利之間夾著阿爾卑斯山與敵意的利古里山道，羅馬不能從北方增援，軍糧靠船，傷兵靠擔架與車隊，山路狹窄處一次只能縱隊行進，兩翼一旦被截斷就難以回援。漢尼拔在意大利的戰場上把羅馬主力釘住，南高盧的守軍只能在沒有後援的狀態下作戰。
tacticsEn: The core of Roman method was the manipular system. The army advanced in two lines of maniples; the front was not a continuous Greek shield wall but a variable formation built from units of a few hundred, and the front rank threw its pila in a mass when the enemy came within about twenty paces, then retired behind the principes to let the sword take over, the two lines relieving one another in turn. In broken country the command changed in the Gallic campaigns of 223 and 222 BC: Postumius Albinus used the cuneus, a dense wedge driving forward in depth, which fitted the narrow defiles and broken slopes of Liguria. Livy records that in 222 BC Rome fought the Ligurians nine times in a single season, working from the coastal hills to the mountain camp and ending with a night attack that carried the camp by surprise, the fires put to the enemy's equipment before the Roman withdrawal, rather than a frontal collision with a fortified position. The Gauls and the Boii fought the opposite way, pressing forward in a dense mass and swinging the long swords around the edge of the shield, and the Roman answer was the massed pilum and the close column, not a battle line extended for the sake of appearance. The decisive variable was supply: between the Narbonensis front and Italy lay the Alps and a hostile line of Ligurian tracks, so no reinforcement could come from the north; grain came by ship, wounded went back on stretchers and wagons, and a narrow defile admitted one column at a time, so a flank once cut could hardly be recovered. Hannibal pinned the Roman main army in Italy, and the southern Gaulian garrisons fought with no prospect of relief.
data: 可核對的數字不多，但足以勾勒戰役規模。前225年兩位執政官各率一支大軍；按波里比烏記載的編制，公民兵團一個約四千二百名步兵、三百名騎兵，加上拉丁同盟與各行省輔兵，每支執政官軍的實力約兩萬人，全線投入南高盧的兵力大致在四萬上下，但各次戰鬥中真正投入山區的顯然只是其中一部分。前223年波里比烏記載阿爾比努斯俘獲七百五十名敵軍，是這條戰線上最具體的一組數字。前222年，李維與波里比烏都提到羅馬在同一季內與利古里人接戰九場，並在季末奪下敵營。李維記載前225年三百零六名法比烏斯族人在克雷梅拉河全滅，這是本戰線最慘重的單一損失，但屬家族傳說，年代與地點都有爭議。戰役的時間跨度是前225至前222年的三個戰役季；把它放回大戰局看，前222年底的特雷比亞河、前216年的坎尼，羅馬在意大利損失的都是以萬計的野戰軍，前225年南高盧這邊的傷亡數字卻沒有留下來——羅馬人一再避免與北方山民正面硬拼，也沒有為一座沒有城牆的營寨投入攻城兵力。
dataEn: Not many figures can be checked, but they are enough to show the scale. In 225 BC each consul led one army; on Polybius's figures a citizen legion was about four thousand two hundred foot and three hundred horse, and once the Latin League and the provincial auxiliaries were added, a consular army came to roughly twenty thousand men, with perhaps forty thousand in all committed on the southern Gaulian line, of which only part was ever committed to the hills. Polybius records that in 223 BC Albinus captured seven hundred and fifty prisoners, the most concrete figure attached to this front. Both Livy and Polybius note that in 222 BC Rome fought the Ligurians nine times in that one season and carried their camp at the end of it. Livy records the deaths of three hundred and six Fabii at the Cremera in 225 BC, the heaviest single loss on this front, though it belongs to family tradition and its date and place are disputed. The campaign ran across three seasons, from 225 to 222 BC. Set beside the wider war, the Trebia at the end of 222 BC and Cannae in 216 BC cost Rome field armies counted in tens of thousands on the Italian side, while the southern Gaulian line left no casualty figures at all: the Romans avoided standing up to the northern hill peoples in the open, and spent no siege labour on a camp without walls.
cause: 南高盧戰爭的直接起因在兩端：一端是利古里人，一端是波河平原。因蘇布列人與波伊人早已不滿羅馬在山南高盧的支配——羅馬的軍隊、移民與道路一直伸到波河平原邊上，兩族擔心阿爾卑斯山另一側的通道被羅馬打通，於是趁羅馬在意大利吃敗仗的時候舉兵，並與越嶺而來的蓋爾人合流。利古里人則長期在阿爾卑斯山與海岸之間的山地劫掠羅馬的盟友與商旅，馬西利亞與其殖民地屢遭襲擊，這是羅馬在意大利之外最沒有退讓餘地的一條線。深層原因在漢尼拔。他要的不是一場高盧人的復仇，而是把羅馬的注意力與兵員釘在北面，讓意大利的正面無法從北方得到任何增援；同時他要在阿爾卑斯山兩側維持一個正在騷動的高盧世界，使羅馬不敢把南高盧行省當作反攻山北的跳板。此外，羅馬在戰略上還有一層被動：前216年坎尼之後，羅馬在意大利的野戰軍幾乎被打空，拉丁同盟人心浮動，羅馬無法抽調精銳，只能靠執政官軍輪番征戰、以防守為主——南高盧戰爭正是在這樣的背景下被迫同時開打。
causeEn: The immediate cause lay at both ends of the front. The Insubres and the Boii had long been hostile to Roman dominance in Cisalpine Gaul: Roman troops, settlers and roads had been pushing towards the edge of the Po plain, and the two peoples feared that a route over the Alps would be opened against them, so they rose while Rome was losing in Italy and joined the Gauls who came over the mountains. The Ligurians, for their part, had long raided the allies and caravans of the Roman client cities in the mountains between the Alps and the coast, and Massalia with its colonies was attacked repeatedly; this was the one front outside Italy where Rome could not afford to give way. The deeper cause was Hannibal. What he wanted was not a Gallic war of revenge but a war that would pin Roman attention and troops in the north, so that the Italian front could draw no reinforcement from that quarter, and he needed the world on both sides of the Alps to stay turbulent so that Rome would not dare to use the province of southern Gaul as a springboard against the mountains. There was a further strategic helplessness: after Cannae in 216 BC the Roman field army in Italy had been all but wiped out and the Latin League was unsettled, so Rome could not detach its best troops and had to fight with consular armies rotated through the front, on the defensive. The war in southern Gaul was forced on Rome alongside that one.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接後果，是羅馬把南高盧線上的主動權握回手裡：前222年沿海道路修通後，羅馬的補給與援軍可以沿海北上，不必再翻山；與馬西利亞的同盟也更加牢固，希臘城邦繼續做羅馬在北方的耳目與海軍基地。往遠看，這條線是羅馬後來征服山南高盧的模板——羅馬先在行省裡修路、設驛站、收編地方首領，然後才在有補給依托的地區作戰，前225至前222年的做法在後來對波伊人、對利古里人的戰爭中一再重演，直到前191年最後一個波伊人首領被徹底消滅、前167年利古里人最後的抵抗結束，羅馬才把目光移向更北的高盧。另一層影響在兵制上：三次山區戰役暴露了手握式縱隊制的極限，丘陵、退路、海上補給都要專門的應對，羅馬在這幾年裡反覆改進分隊的編制、徵用馬西利亞的騎兵與希臘式標槍兵，這些細碎調整後來都寫進了軍制的習慣裡。就史料而言，這場戰爭留下兩部主要記載：波里比烏第二卷講北方戰線，李維第五卷用最沉重的筆墨寫法比烏斯家族的覆滅與執政官的困境，兩相比照，恰好顯示羅馬人自己怎麼理解前225年前後那幾年。
impactEn: The immediate effect of the war was that Rome took the initiative back on the southern line: once the coastal road was open in 222 BC, supply and reinforcements could move north along the shore instead of over the mountains, and the alliance with Massalia grew tighter, with the Greek cities remaining Rome's eyes and ears and naval base in the north. In the longer run this line became the template for the Roman conquest of Cisalpine Gaul: first roads, staging posts and client chiefs in the province, then campaigning from a place where the army could be supplied, and the practice of 225 to 222 BC was repeated in the later wars against the Boii and the Ligurians, until the last Boii leader was destroyed in 191 BC and the last Ligurian resistance ended in 167 BC, and Rome's gaze moved further north. A second effect was institutional: three mountain campaigns showed the limits of the manipular system, since broken ground, withdrawal routes and a sea-borne supply each needed their own answers, and the Romans repeatedly adjusted the size of their units and drew on Massalian cavalry and Greek-style javelin men, small adjustments that hardened into habit. For the record, two principal narratives survive: Polybius' second book for the northern front, and Livy's fifth book, written in the heaviest register for the destruction of the Fabii and the predicament of the consuls; read against each other they show how the Romans themselves understood those few years around 225 BC.
result: 前225年的戰役以一個不體面的僵局收場：利古里人在沿海丘陵被羅馬打敗，執政官軍卻在波河平原的入口被波伊人、因蘇布列人與蓋爾人聯軍擋住，只得分隊退回南高盧行省，掩住通往山北的通道。僵局在前223年鬆動：阿爾比努斯打散波伊人與因蘇布列人的聯軍，俘獲七百五十人，逼得蓋爾人退回山嶺那邊；前222年羅馬奪下克拉斯提迪烏姆，佔住波河平原的西端，再以一季九戰掃平利古里人的抵抗，奪營焚燒其器材，並在沿海修通道路。北方線於是安靜下來，羅馬得以把注意力收回意大利。真正的勝負並不在南高盧：前222年底的特雷比亞河與前216年的坎尼，仍是漢尼拔用高盧與伊比利亞部隊擊敗羅馬主力，羅馬在南高盧守住的這道門，恰好是把意大利暴露在高盧兵鋒之下的那一道。從更長的視角看，這三場戰爭是羅馬學會如何對付北方的前奏：南高盧的羅馬人靠道路、海軍與地方盟友取勝，山北的波伊人則要等到前191年才被消滅。
resultEn: The campaign of 225 BC ended in an unflattering stalemate. The Ligurians were beaten in the coastal hills, but the consular armies were shut out of the entrance to the Po plain by the Boii, the Insubres and the Gallic coalition, and had to fall back in detachments into the province of southern Gaul, holding the road north. The stalemate loosened in 223 BC, when Albinus broke up the Boii and Insubrian coalition and took seven hundred and fifty prisoners, driving the Gauls back over the mountains; in 222 BC Rome took Clastidium, holding the western end of the Po plain, then settled the Ligurian resistance in nine engagements in a single season, carrying the camp, burning its equipment and opening the coastal road. The northern line then went quiet and Rome could turn its attention back to Italy. The real decision was not taken in southern Gaul: at the Trebia at the end of 222 BC and at Cannae in 216 BC, Hannibal's Gallic and Iberian troops still destroyed the Roman main army, and the door Rome held in southern Gaul was precisely the one that left Italy open to the Gallic sword. On the longer view these three campaigns were the rehearsal for learning to fight the north: in southern Gaul the Romans won with roads, sea power and local allies, while the Boii north of the mountains were not destroyed until 191 BC.
